name: mid-analyst-to-ml-stretch
note: Terse resume. A business analyst who does real SQL and dashboards, reaching for a machine learning engineer role. A stretch: the data literacy transfers, the modelling, Python engineering and production ML do not. The expected score is low and the guard should stop any attempt to dress BI work up as ML.

jd_text:
Machine Learning Engineer
Remote (US) | Applied ML | $160,000 - $200,000

We are building fraud detection for a payments network that moves about $9 billion a year.
The applied ML group is seven engineers. Models we ship make automated decisions on live
transactions in under 80 milliseconds, and a bad model costs real money in both directions:
fraud we let through and good customers we block.

What you will do
- Own fraud models end to end: problem framing, feature development, training, offline
  evaluation, shadow deployment, and production monitoring
- Build and maintain feature pipelines in Python and Spark over a feature store, with the
  training and serving paths sharing the same feature definitions
- Deploy models as low-latency services and be responsible for their latency budget
- Design and run online experiments, and defend the results when they are inconvenient
- Monitor for drift and decide when a model needs retraining rather than waiting for a
  quarterly cadence
- Work with the fraud operations team, who will tell you things the data does not

Required
- 3+ years building machine learning systems that ran in production and affected real
  decisions. Notebooks and internal proofs of concept are not what we mean
- Strong Python engineering: you write testable modules, not scripts
- Deep familiarity with gradient boosted trees (XGBoost, LightGBM) and when a neural
  approach is or is not worth the operational cost
- Solid grounding in evaluation: precision-recall tradeoffs at extreme class imbalance,
  calibration, and why accuracy is the wrong metric here
- Feature engineering on transactional and time-series data, including leakage avoidance
- Experience with a distributed compute framework, Spark or Ray
- MLflow or another experiment tracking discipline you actually kept up
- SQL at a level where a complex warehouse query is unremarkable

Nice to have
- Fraud, risk, credit or another adversarial domain where the data distribution fights back
- Feature store experience: Feast, Tecton or an in-house equivalent
- Real-time inference at single-digit millisecond budgets
- Graph features or entity resolution
- Kubernetes, Docker, and enough infrastructure comfort to debug your own deployment
- Causal inference

We do not require a PhD, and we do not ask algorithm puzzle questions. The technical rounds
are a modelling design discussion on one of our real problems and a Python engineering pair
session.
